The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

answer.feedback: No candidate meets the acceptance criteria. Search for a substrate-dependent uptake/growth mechanism that can capture the differing substrate residuals across experiments. The inhibition candidates still over-predict x2 in E2 near t=2 h, but under-predict x2 in E1 near t=2 h and E3 near t=15 h. The simpler Contois and Monod candidates also under-predict x2 in E2 near t=3 h and E3 at t=20 h. Check the feed profiles to identify whether these discrepancies occur at high or low substrate; the diagnostics provided do not state the actual substrate regimes. In particular, test whether the uptake response changes across those regimes rather than assuming one inhibition shape.
answer.reasoning: C40 has the highest Akaike weight, but its chi2 (530.2) is far above the 95% limit (147.7), and KS and Ki are strongly correlated. The other candidates also fail the fit limit; C18 additionally has an unestimated parameter. Thus none fits within noise with all parameters precisely estimated.
